questions.q: The meeting is ___ 3 o'clock.
questions.why: Use 'at' with clock times.

questions.q: My birthday is ___ July.
questions.why: Use 'in' with months and years.

questions.q: We always rest ___ Sunday.
questions.why: Use 'on' with days and dates.

questions.q: Please finish the report ___ Friday at the latest.
questions.why: 'By' means no later than a deadline; 'until' means up to that point continuously.

questions.q: I will wait here ___ you arrive.
questions.why: 'Until' marks a continuous action up to a point in time.

questions.q: She studied ___ three hours last night.
questions.why: Use 'for' with a length of time.

questions.q: He fell asleep ___ the film.
questions.why: Use 'during' with a noun naming an event or period.

questions.q: I have lived here ___ 2015.
questions.why: Use 'since' with a starting point in time.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'The train leaves ___ noon.'
questions.why: Use 'at' with specific points of time like noon and midnight.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'We met ___ 2020, and we are still friends.'
questions.why: Use 'in' with years.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I have not seen her ___ Monday.'
questions.why: Use 'since' with a point that marks the start of a period continuing to now.

questions.q: There is a lamp ___ the table.
questions.why: Use 'on' for a surface contact.

questions.q: The keys are ___ my pocket.
questions.why: Use 'in' for being inside an enclosed space.

questions.q: I will meet you ___ the bus stop.
questions.why: Use 'at' for a specific point or location.

questions.q: A plane flew ___ the city without landing.
questions.why: 'Over' suggests movement across or directly above; here the plane passes across the city.

questions.q: The temperature is two degrees ___ zero.
questions.why: Use 'above' for a higher level on a scale, with no contact or movement.

questions.q: She sat ___ Tom and Mary.
questions.why: Use 'between' for two distinct people or things.

questions.q: He was happy to be ___ friends again.
questions.why: Use 'among' for being in the middle of a group of three or more.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'The picture hangs ___ the wall.'
questions.why: Use 'on' for contact with a vertical surface.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Divide the cake ___ the two children.'
questions.why: Use 'between' when there are exactly two recipients.

questions.q: She is very good ___ mathematics.
questions.why: 'Good at' is a fixed dependent preposition for skills.

questions.q: I am interested ___ learning Spanish.
questions.why: 'Interested in' is the fixed dependent preposition.

questions.q: Our plans depend ___ the weather.
questions.why: 'Depend on' is fixed; never 'depend of'.

questions.q: Many children are afraid ___ the dark.
questions.why: 'Afraid of' is the fixed dependent preposition.

questions.q: She has been married ___ him for ten years.
questions.why: 'Married to' is fixed; never 'married with'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'He is not very good ___ cooking.'
questions.why: 'Good at' is used for abilities and activities.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'This success depends ___ hard work.'
questions.why: 'Depend on' is the correct collocation.

questions.q: I usually go to work ___ car.
questions.why: Use 'by' with means of transport: by car, by train, by plane.

questions.q: It is healthy to go to school ___ foot.
questions.why: The fixed exception is 'on foot', not 'by foot'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'We travelled across the country ___ train.'
questions.why: Use 'by' for modes of transport.
